0.long_answer: The disease in question is sarcoidosis. This condition was first described in 1877 by the English doctor Jonathan Hutchinson. Sarcoidosis is characterized by abnormal collections of inflammatory cells, primarily macrophages, which form granulomas. These granulomas typically appear in organs such as the lungs, skin, or lymph nodes, although they can affect almost any organ in the body. Over time, the granulomatous inflammation may lead to varying degrees of organ dysfunction depending on which tissues are involved.
